2028 Mitsubishi Outlander Diamond Trail Edition: How Does It Compare to Other Adventure Crossovers?
14 photos
Photo: Mitsubishi
Mitsubishi Motors North America ( MMNA ) revealed ahead of the 2026 edition of the SEMA Show (November 3 to 6) its triumphant return to Las Vegas, Nevada, for the first time since 2012. The Japanese company’s subsidiary also has a headline – the 2028 Outlander Diamond Trail Edition.
We’ve said it on numerous occasions: quite sadly, right now the Japanese automaker’s US subsidiary is a pale shadow of a shadow of its former self . If you need an eloquent example, earlier this month they reported a total of just 18,543 sales during the third quarter of 2026, and after that the only novelty has been the reveal of the pricing details for the Nissan Leaf-based 2027 Mitsubishi Eclipse Sportback. The new fastback EV starts at an MSRP of almost $38k, which is considerably higher than its corporate sibling, which kicks off at less than $30k for the 2026 model year.
Most likely they won’t improve their sales too much with this new model, but at least we have higher hopes for the new 2028 Outlander Diamond Trail Edition , which is an adventure version of their best-selling nameplate. The trail-focused version of its three-row crossover is coming as a triple example at the SEMA Show, one stock with Mitsubishi Genuine Accessories and a color-matched Thule roof box, one packing more goodies, and the third one as extreme as possible.
Back to the regular version, the new trim levels come with a new Rock off-road mode for the Super-All Wheel Control System, modified bumpers which enable improved approach and departure angles from 18.3 to 20.5 degrees and from 22.2 to 23.1 degrees, all-terrain tires, and new wheels: 18-inch black alloy wheels with dedicated Nexen Roadian ATXs.
Photo: Mitsubishi Inside, there’s off-road feedback through the dedicated instrument-cluster display screen in Rock mode, showing things like the steering angle, individual wheel slip, and traction-control intervention in real time, while the Multi-View Camera System also acts differently and stays active up to 18.6 mph or 30 kph instead of the standard 6.2mph/10kph threshold.
There is also a unique water-repelling dark grey material with khaki stitching for the upholstery, as well as textured matte black, dark chrome, and dark satin trim elements. The new Diamond Trail Edition logo is also present, on the seat backs, floor mats, and the door card. Last but not least, Mitsubishi introduces a new color, Trail Green Metallic, highlighting the Diamond Trail Edition.
Mitsubishi hasn’t revealed any additional technical characteristics or the pricing details and the release date, but we can easily see the 2028 model year of the Mitsubishi Outlander take on the flurry of compact crossover SUV adventurers like the Ford Bronco Sport Badlands, Jeep Compass Trailhawk, Toyota RAV4 Woodland, Honda CR-V TrailSport Hybrid, Hyundai Tucson XRT, Kia Sportage X-Pro, Subaru Forester Wilderness, and also the Nissan Rogue Rock Creek Edition, of course.
Photo: Mitsubishi All of them come with a ton of adventure-focused tips and tricks. The Nissan Rogue Rock Creek has standard AWD, exclusive styling perks, water-repellent seats, HDC, and an HD Intelligent Around View Monitor, among other things, with the standard 1.5-liter VC-Turbo 3-cylinder engine still packed under the hood with 201 hp and 225 lb-ft of torque.
The Toyota RAV4 Woodland is even more capable than the Nissan because it has a standard 236-hp hybrid powertrain and the optional 324-hp plug-in hybrid option. It also comes with rugged features: increased ground clearance, a TRD-tuned suspension, all-terrain tires, and 18-inch wheels. The Hyundai Tucson XRT is also available as a hybrid and leans heavily into the adventure look from the get-go, but you should always also consider its sibling, the Kia Sportage X-Pro (gasoline) or Sportage X-Line Hybrid, before making a choice.
We shouldn’t forget about the newly introduced Honda CR-V TrailSport Hybrid or the recently launched Subaru Forester Wilderness, which is now also available with the hybrid powertrain, or about the American greats, the Ford Bronco Sport Badlands and the Jeep Cherokee Trailhawk Hybrid. One thing is for sure: the 2028 Mitsubishi Outlander Diamond Trail Edition will have its work cut out for it because most carmakers offer an adventure-focused version of their most popular compact crossover SUVs across the US automotive market right now.
Photo: Mitsubishi Interestingly, we don’t believe that Mitsubishi chose the SEMA Show in Las Vegas for nothing, as the stock example is joined by another two units that feature increasingly complicated off-road-focused configurations with extra goodies from across the aftermarket realm. The second Mitsu BF Goodrich Trail Terrain T/A tires sized 265/65-18, a Thule Caprock roof rack packing two Specialized StumpJumper 15 mountain bikes, as well as an Anderson Design & Fabrication 1.5-inch lift kit.
There’s also accessory lighting from Rough Country, as well as a matching custom-painted GulfStream Trail Boss 1090K trailer. The third one is even more extreme, packing 18 by 8.5-inch Method Race Wheels 707s, T/A K03s, a 2.5-inch suspension lift via Flatout Suspension's GR Lite strut kit with adjustable spring perches, a Thule Caprock roof rack topped with a Thule Approach 2M rooftop tent and Rough Country traction boards, plus a Rough Country accessory light bar and light pods.
